Ribbon convention: the iron-framed shop, mezzanine and the two glazed storeys are divided only by iron posts and colonnettes under 0.3 m, so each is one opening per band.

facades.name: Herengracht store front
facades.note: Cropped to the glazing between the two glazed-brick piers (alongM from the stuccoed house's east end, the face's viewer-left edge: piers at 5.4-6.65 and 17.0-18.2). Bands from the bottom: shop windows, small-pane mezzanine, first glazed storey, second glazed storey (segmental heads), six attic windows, the rooftop glazing over the cornice. The shop band is three openings: the display windows stand between broad dark iron piers (about 0.4 m in the aimed view, wider than the 0.3 m ribbon gap). Axes: the three glazed bays' centres do not line up with the six attic windows, so the photo has nine distinct axes.

facades.name: Leidsestraat front
facades.note: Bands from the bottom: shop windows, mezzanine, the two glazed storeys in three bays, eight attic windows; the 2022 look shows no rooftop glazing over this cornice. alongM from the face's viewer-left silhouette edge, which is the Herengracht store's side seen edge-on beyond the rounded corner, to the inner faces of the two end piers (7.85-19.8 m). The shop band is three openings between broad dark iron piers (2022 look). Axes: the eight attic windows plus the middle bay's centre, which falls between two attic windows (the outer bay centres fall within 0.3 m of an attic axis): nine.
